context:
Goal: the env-file guard stops refusing a python or node heredoc whose text only names an env file, without letting real env reads through.
Problem (rule): a held change waits for your word. #2315 fixes that false alarm but opens 4 rare holes and closes 1, so round 3 found its net value negative (reviewer sonnet).
Based on (measured): round 3 at c62328127. The 4 holes: a nested template literal in a node heredoc; an interpreter word anywhere before `<<` (such as `cat > node/go <<'EOF'`); a python triple-quoted string that holds `$(`; a node regex with // inside a character class.
Departs from: main refuses those heredocs as env reads — a new lane would allow heredocs that only name an env file in text, and keep refusing real reads.
Meanwhile: nothing runs on #2315.

options.gain: The false alarm goes, and the two new holes those narrowings target close.
options.how: The new lane matches the interpreter only as the heredoc's command word, and stops blanking text after a nested backtick.
options.label: New lane at round 1, with two narrowings

options.how: Close #2315 and add the false alarm under the decision's Known false alarms.
options.label: Drop #2315 and list the false alarm

reply: Routed 18:40 CST Nov 8 to step env-heredoc-name-in-prose, roadmap 19ac3b6d8: the coordinator starts a new lane at round 1 with the two narrowings; #2315 joins the close list when the new PR exists.
title: #2315 is held after round 3: run a new lane with two narrowings, or drop it and list the false alarm?
